<reason>Side A built a logically airtight case around the inescapable geometry of finite urban land and systematically dismantled every alternative Side B proposed. When Side B retreated to preserving "dedicated sections" for religious in-ground burial, Side A used the Pressure Questions and Closing rounds to force Side B into conceding both halves of the core dilemma: either cannibalizing scarce urban land to expand cemeteries or relying on the exact peri-urban religious cemeteries Side B had previously attacked as inequitable.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>In [A2.1]-[A2.2], Side A dismantled Side B's proposed alternatives to land scarcity by showing that lease-based plot recycling (exhumation) and above-ground mausoleums directly violate the exact Jewish and Muslim covenants for permanent, undisturbed earth burial that Side B's own case rested upon.</best_rebuttal>
